correctness.rationale: A split w=uv makes its proper prefix u a suffix of the rotation vu. Thus no two rotations can appear; any word with a nontrivial rotational stabilizer is self-bordered. Unequal cyclic intermarker gaps select a unique orientation of the shorter gap and hence m² primitive necklaces per shorter distance. For n=2d, the equal-valued antipodal case is periodic. An antipodal word with distinct markers must put a marker at one end to avoid a zero-to-zero length-one border. The two resulting endpoint orientations cannot mix, and length-d comparisons separate the two marker alphabets, giving at most floor(m²/4). In the proposed construction a prefix must contain exactly one marker, so k≤t (the second-marker index of the prefix word), and a suffix needs k≥n−s (s the suffix word's second-marker index). Because s,t≤n/2, only an antipodal half-length comparison is possible, and disjoint alphabets forbid it. This covers all proper lengths and self-overlaps, even when m=1. The claimed deficit is the difference between choose(m,2) and floor(m²/4). Independent replay with literal prefix/suffix union subset search matched all 14 small cases (python3 /workspace/replay/checks.py 3); this is finite corroboration, not the proof.
